about.title: Loyalton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Loyalton is small enough that a death touches everyone. With 769 residents in Sierra County, families here rarely have to think about wrongful death claims, and the public record reflects that: the most recent final crash year, 2025, recorded zero injury collisions and zero traffic deaths. Still, fatal losses do not only come from the road. A fall at work, a preventable medical error, an incident at a business along Church Street or near Courthouse Square, or a collision on Rt 49 or Beckwith Road can all leave a family asking what comes next. California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring a wrongful death claim first, then certain dependents and heirs. The claim is civil and stands apart from any criminal case. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive is not a law firm; we connect you, free, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Loyalton Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can quickly confirm where your family stands before anything else is decided.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but the window is much shorter when a government entity may share responsibility. Connecting early protects that time.

items.title: Every loss accounted for
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the income your loved one would have earned, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance all count under California law. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Loyalton recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Can a wrongful death claim still arise here?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic collisions are only one cause of wrongful death, and a quiet year on Rt 49 or Beckwith Road does not change the law. Deaths from medical negligence, unsafe property, workplace incidents, or defective products can all support a claim, and a death that happens outside city limits may still involve a Loyalton family.

items.question: What if a Sierra County or state vehicle or agency was involved?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two-year deadline, and a formal claim usually has to be filed before any lawsuit. Missing that window can end the case before it begins. An attorney can identify whether a public agency is involved and act on the tighter schedule.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death case is a civil action and proceeds separately from any criminal prosecution in Sierra County. The outcome of the criminal case can matter as evidence, but your family's civil deadline runs regardless of how long the criminal matter takes.
